conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: BreakoutFollowThroughWeaknessBar
candidates.quote: If, instead of having several strong bull trend bars in a row, the bar after a one- or two-bar breakout is a small bar, a doji, an inside bar, a bar with large tails, or a bear trend bar, the breakout might fail.
candidates.description: Filter: the bar right after a short breakout is itself weak (small body, doji, inside bar, large tail, or opposite color) — a sign the breakout may fail.
candidates.pseudocode: (abs(close[0] - open[0]) < bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0])) || (abs(close[0] - open[0]) <= dojiFraction * (high[0] - low[0])) || (high[0] < high[1] && low[0] > low[1]) || (high[0] - maxList(open[0], close[0]) >= tailFraction * (high[0] - low[0])) || (minList(open[0], close[0]) - low[0] >= tailFraction * (high[0] - low[0])) || close[0] < open[0]

complexity.reason: an OR of several single-bar sub-tests

candidates.name: MultipleMeasuredMoveTargetsWatchNearest
candidates.quote: there are usually several possibilities for the measurement points and it is best to watch the nearest target first ... Once that measured move was exceeded, traders should look at other possibilities.
candidates.description: When several measured-move candidates (open-to-close, open-to-high, low-to-close, low-to-high of the spike, all projected forward) are in play, take profits at whichever untouched target is nearest, then move on to the next one.
candidates.pseudocode: targets = { openToCloseTarget, openToHighTarget, lowToCloseTarget, lowToHighTarget }; nearestUntouched = min(t in targets where t > close[0]); high[0] >= nearestUntouched - toleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: profit-taking limit at each successive projection

complexity.reason: requires computing and ranking several measured-move anchors simultaneously and tracking which have already been reached

notes: Ties together RP1-07, R02-34 and other single-anchor measured-move candidates as alternative targets rather than one fixed target.

candidates.name: WedgeMeasuredMoveTarget
candidates.quote: The market tried to form a wedge bear flag beginning at the bar 4 low, and it had three pushes up ... Using the bar 4 low to the top of the wedge for the measurement projected a move that was exceeded by only one tick at the bar 14 high of the day.
candidates.description: After a failed three-push wedge, project a measured move from the wedge's start low to its top, added again above the top.
candidates.pseudocode: wedgeStart = low[s]; wedgeTop = highest(high, wedgeBars)[e]; target = wedgeTop + (wedgeTop - wedgeStart); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: needs three-push wedge recognition and remembered start/top levels

notes: Related to R02-37's three-push channel primitive.

candidates.name: BreakevenStopAfterProfitThreshold
candidates.quote: Once bar 14 hit five ticks above the long entry, many bulls moved their stops to breakeven
candidates.description: Once open profit reaches a fixed tick threshold, move the protective stop to the entry price.
candidates.book_order_type: move the resting stop-loss order to the entry price

complexity.reason: a single open-profit comparison against a fixed threshold

notes: Distinct from the catalog's ProfitProtector (a proportional-giveback trail): this is a one-time breakeven move triggered at a fixed profit level, not tied to a peak or a retracement ratio.

candidates.name: ShortFadeAtThirdPushWedgeHigh
candidates.quote: Bar 15 was a bad signal for longs, who expected that any rally would end below the bar 14 wedge high ... Aggressive traders shorted above its high, because a buy signal that is likely to fail means that traders could go short.
candidates.description: When a buy setup forms right at a third-push wedge high in a strong trend, fade it: short above the failing buy signal bar's high rather than buying it.
candidates.pseudocode: pushCount(channelLookback, pivotStrength) >= 3 && high[0] <= wedgeHigh + toleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop above the failing long signal bar's high

complexity.reason: needs three-push/wedge recognition to identify the failing signal bar's context

candidates.name: DojiSignalBarLessReliable
candidates.quote: doji bars are not reliable signal bars
candidates.description: Filter: a doji bar is a weaker signal bar than a trend bar; reduce confidence in (or skip) entries whose signal bar is a doji.

candidates.name: TrappedBuyerStopRunShort
candidates.quote: Bar 1 was a strong bull trend bar that trapped early buyers ... A buy was not even triggered on this 5 minute chart, since the next bar did not go above the bar 1 high ... Place an order to short on a stop at one tick below the low of bar 1, which is where those longs will have their protective stops.
candidates.description: After a strong trend bar fails to trigger its own continuation (the next bar never exceeds its high), place a sell stop just below its low to catch the stop-running liquidation of the traders trapped long inside it.
candidates.pseudocode: close[1] > open[1] && (close[1] - open[1]) >= bodyFraction * (high[1] - low[1]) && high[0] <= high[1]
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop one tick below the trapping bar's low

complexity.reason: a two-bar structural test with a remembered trapping-bar low used as the stop level

candidates.name: Barbwire
candidates.quote: Bar 5 is the third overlapping bar and at least one of the bars was a doji (all three were). This is barbwire, which is usually a continuation pattern
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a short run of small, heavily overlapping bars including at least one doji — a tight, directionless micro-range Brooks calls barbwire.
candidates.pseudocode: countIf(i in [0, barbwireBars - 1): (minList(high[i], high[i + 1]) - maxList(low[i], low[i + 1])) >= overlapThreshold * (high[i + 1] - low[i + 1]), barbwireBars - 1) >= barbwireBars - 1 && existsDoji(barbwireBars, dojiFraction)

complexity.reason: a windowed overlap test combined with an existence scan for a doji, over a variable-length recent run

candidates.name: FadeSmallBarAtBarbwireExtreme
candidates.quote: like with any trading range, you should never buy at its high or sell at its low. You can fade small bars at its extremes
candidates.description: Inside barbwire, fade (short) a small bar that trades up to the range's recent high, or fade (buy) one that trades down to its recent low.
candidates.pseudocode: Barbwire[0] && (high[0] - low[0]) <= smallBarAtr * atr(atrLookback) && close[0] >= highest(high, barbwireBars)[0] - toleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop or limit near the range extreme

complexity.reason: an ATR-relative bar-size test layered on the barbwire primitive

candidates.name: FinalFlagFailedBreakoutReversal
candidates.quote: since all horizontal trading ranges are magnets and often become final flags, you can wait for a trend bar breakout to fail and look for a reversal back into the range.
candidates.description: Filter/context: a horizontal micro-range (barbwire) late in a trend is a candidate final flag; wait for a breakout attempt out of it to fail and re-enter in the opposite (reversal) direction.
candidates.pseudocode: Barbwire[1] && ((close[1] > highest(high, barbwireBars)[2] && close[0] < highest(high, barbwireBars)[2]))

complexity.reason: 'final flag' recognition and what counts as a failed breakout both require design decisions

candidates.name: ReversalBarMinimumCloseAboveMidpoint
candidates.quote: bar 7 closed above its midpoint and therefore met the minimum requirement for a reversal bar
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the minimum bar-level test for a bull reversal bar is simply that it closed in the upper half of its own range.
notes: At threshold=0.5 this is exactly CloseRangePosition's test.

candidates.name: CandlestickTrapFade
candidates.quote: When you see these small-bodied big candles in a strong trend where there has yet to be a trend line break, you should get excited because they are great traps and therefore perfect short setups.
candidates.description: In an intact bear trend (no trend-line break yet), a large-range, small-bodied bar with a long tail against the trend (a classic bullish 'hammer'/reversal candle) is a trap; fade it by placing an entry stop right where the trapped counter-trend traders' protective stops sit (beyond the tail).
candidates.pseudocode: !majorTrendLineBroken && (minList(open[0], close[0]) - low[0]) >= tailFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && abs(close[0] - open[0]) <= smallBodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0])
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop one tick below the trap bar's low

complexity.reason: the bar test itself is simple, but 'no trend line break yet' is a persistent trend-line-projection state

candidates.name: InsideBodyBar
candidates.quote: it was an inside body variant (its body was inside the body of the signal bar, which is a weaker version of an inside bar)
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a weaker variant of an inside bar where only the body (not the full high-low range) sits inside the prior bar's body.
candidates.pseudocode: maxList(open[0], close[0]) < maxList(open[1], close[1]) && minList(open[0], close[0]) > minList(open[1], close[1])
notes: The catalog's InsideBar uses high/low containment; this variant uses body containment and is explicitly weaker.

candidates.name: ExpectStopRunBeforeSecondLeg
candidates.quote: It is reasonable to assume that there will be two legs up, but almost certainly there will be a stop run down before the second leg.
candidates.description: Filter/context: after the first leg of a two-legged move, expect a brief counter-trend stop run before the second leg begins; avoid treating that stop run as a trend reversal.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter; do not exit/reverse on the expected stop run)

complexity.reason: leg counting and 'stop run' both lack an agreed mechanical definition

candidates.name: OutsideBarResetsLegCounter
candidates.quote: Whenever there is a strong outside up bar that breaks the market into a new trend, its low is the start of the trend and all bar counting gets reset. For example, the two-bar reversal at bar 9 was a low 1 setup and not a low 2.
candidates.description: When a strong outside bar breaks the market into a new trend, reset any pullback/leg counter (H1/H2, L1/L2 style) so the outside bar's extreme becomes the new trend start.
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] > high[1] && low[0] < low[1] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) => pullbackCounter = 0; trendStartLow = low[0]

complexity.reason: an outside-bar test that also mutates persistent counter state used elsewhere

rejected.quote: You will regularly hear pundits discuss a one- or two-day sell-off in a stock that resulted from a bad report, like a disappointing earnings report or a change in management.
rejected.reason: requires news/fundamental data the engine does not have; the chapter's own conclusion is to trade the chart instead

rejected.quote: some news must have been released that led to a sharp sell-off at 10:30 a.m. PST. You should never pay attention to the news
rejected.reason: requires news event data, which the engine does not have and which Brooks himself says to ignore

rejected.quote: You must always consider both bull and bear alternatives.
rejected.reason: pure discretion with no bar-level test

chapter_summary: Chapter 3 walks three intraday charts and yields a mix of genuinely new mechanics beyond the signs-of-strength checklist: a breakeven-stop-at-fixed-profit rule, a trapped-buyer stop-run short, the barbwire micro-range primitive with its fade-the-extremes and final-flag-reversal filters, a body-only 'inside body' bar variant, a candlestick-trap fade that requires an intact trend line, an outside-bar leg-counter reset, and a 'watch the nearest of several measured-move targets' meta-rule. Two 'watch the chart, not the news' passages and one generic discretion line were rejected. Several ideas (three-push wedge/channel measured moves, third-consecutive-climax corrections, trend-line-break-enables-countertrend) restate concepts already mined in RP1, R01, and R02 and should be merged in the dedup pass.
